verses.text: When Yahweh your God cuts off the nations, whose land Yahweh your God gives you, and you succeed them, and dwell in their cities, and in their houses;
you shall set apart three cities for yourselves in the middle of your land, which Yahweh your God gives you to possess it.
You shall prepare the way, and divide the borders of your land, which Yahweh your God causes you to inherit, into three parts, that every man slayer may flee there.
This is the case of the man slayer who shall flee there and live. Whoever kills his neighbor unawares, and didn’t hate him in time past;

as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to chop wood, and his hand fetches a stroke with the ax to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle, and lights on his neighbor, so that he dies, he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the man slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and strike him mortally; even though he was not worthy of death, because he didn’t hate him in time past.
Therefore I command you to set apart three cities for yourselves.
If Yahweh your God enlarges your border, as he has sworn to your fathers, and gives you all the land which he promised to give to your fathers;
if you keep all this commandment to do it, which I command you today, to love Yahweh your God, and to walk ever in his ways; then you shall add three cities more for yourselves, besides these three.
This is so that innocent blood will not be shed in the middle of your land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance, leaving blood guilt on you.
But if any man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises up against him, strikes him mortally so that he dies, and he flees into one of these cities;
then the elders of his city shall send and bring him there, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.
Your eye shall not pity him, but you shall purge the innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with you.
You shall not remove your neighbor’s landmark, which they of old time have set, in your inheritance which you shall inherit, in the land that Yahweh your God gives you to possess.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter be established.
If an unrighteous witness rises up against any man to testify against him of wrongdoing,
then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges who shall be in those days;
and the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness is a false witness, and has testified falsely against his brother;
then you shall do to him as he had thought to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
Those who remain shall hear, and fear, and will never again commit any such evil among you.
Your eyes shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

footnotes.content: God is already working it out before you arrive—He cuts off the nations, then settles you in their land. Long before you take a single step into the promised country, He has prepared the way. This is the heart of it: your inheritance isn't something you seize; it's something the Lord makes ready and gives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three cities of refuge—a safety net woven into the fabric of the nation itself. God isn't just giving land; He's building mercy into the law from the start. Every structure, every boundary, every city is an act of foresight and love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Prepare the way"—the roads matter as much as the cities. When someone flees in panic after a terrible accident, the way itself becomes a mercy. God cares about the distance, the clarity, the accessibility. Compassion includes the details.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice the words: "unawares" and "didn't hate him in time past." God reads the heart. A death by accident carries a weight different from murder. The law protects not just the guilty from false accusation, but the innocent from unnecessary blood-guilt. There is wisdom in distinction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two men in the forest, an axe, a slip—and a life ends. The picture is brutally ordinary: the hand fetches a stroke, the head slips, and sorrow spreads like spilled blood. For the man whose ax head flies, this city of refuge is a door between death and a second chance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The avenger of blood is human, and human hearts run hot when grief is fresh. The law makes room for this: the way is long enough for anger to cool, reason to return. Even in justice, God builds in space for mercy to work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I command you." The safety system doesn't arise from accident; it comes from explicit, deliberate command. Moses speaks with the weight of God behind him. This protection is no afterthought—it is law, carved into the structure of the nation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If the Lord enlarges your border—notice the condition rests on His oath to the fathers and His gift of the land. Expansion is not conquest but fulfillment of promise. And with enlargement comes a new question: how will mercy grow?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Love Yahweh your God, walk in His ways—and then add three more cities. Obedience and mercy are linked. As the people grow in faith, the system of refuge grows too. Faithfulness to God expands faithfulness to neighbor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Innocent blood will not be shed." The cities of refuge exist to prevent further tragedy, to halt the cascade of revenge that turns one death into a dynasty of grief. Justice without these cities becomes a wheel that never stops turning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the text turns sharp: "If any man hates his neighbor, lies in wait." This is murder—premeditated, full of malice. The law has drawn a line between the man whose ax slipped and the man whose hatred lay waiting in darkness for its moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The elders don't hide the guilty; they bring him out and deliver him to the avenger of blood. Justice does not hide behind the city of refuge. The city shelters only the innocent. The guilty stand exposed and accountable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Your eye shall not pity him."—A hard word. Yet it protects Israel itself. When a nation allows the guilty to walk unpunished, blood-guilt settles on the whole people, like a weight that never lifts. Justice and purity are bound together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your neighbor's landmark—those old stones set by ancestors to mark the boundary. To move them is to steal not just land but history, trust, and the order your forebears built. Small sins carry their own weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "One witness shall not rise up." The law requires two or three—a shield against the lie told in secret, the false accusation whispered in shadows. The innocent are protected not by luck but by law: a threshold that guards truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An unrighteous witness—a person willing to stand and lie, to swear falsely against another. This is poison in the well of justice. The text pauses here to single out this evil, this perversion of the very court meant to protect innocence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Both men stand before Yahweh, before priests and judges. The dispute is elevated beyond human squabbling—it's brought into the presence of God. The court is a sacred space where truth is meant to emerge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The judges make diligent inquisition—they dig, they examine, they don't rush. When a false witness is found, his lie is exposed. Truth has a way of rising to the surface when seekers are patient and careful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Do to him as he had thought to do to his brother." The false witness wanted to destroy an innocent man; he receives what he intended for another. There's a mirror held up here—the harm we plan often becomes the harm we reap.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: "Those who remain shall hear, and fear." Justice that is clear and kept teaches the whole people. In our age of hidden consequences and muted accountability, we still need to see the link between violation and reckoning—so that fear of the Lord returns to the land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Your eyes shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth." This talion principle—measure for measure—stops escalation. It says: the wound matches the crime, no more, no less. Proportionality is mercy's shield against endless vengeance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
